review: It's alright.

While in a Metroidvania mood, I decided to pick this up after previously giving up on it out of annoyance. Now, I did get further and, for a while, actually enjoyed it. Then I discovered you can only get certain items beating boss fights without being hit, forcing you to be perfect for trinkets that could actually help you progress.

Okay, I could live with that I guess. Annoying, but possible.

Then the mine level happened. Pixel perfect jumps or you instantly die, an annoying turret section which you have no hope of finishing unharmed, followed by more instant death jumps, and a boost function I never even saw, ALL of which while you collect relic pieces you see for a NANO second between blind leaps of faith and hitting enemies that'll hurt you if you don't jump into them, and two achievements tied to a perfect run.

And they follow this up with a hotel level that demands you attack enemies coming from multiple angles while also dodging a space laser. And then has an elevator section that demands perfection for another achievement, despite it being the cheapest attacks ever (I got hit and lost health MID-KILLING THE ENEMY THAT DID IT).

I was prepared to be annoyed by this, because that's always the case with Metroidvanias, they are blood boilingly annoying at times, but between the design and feeling like my character is always jumping, running and attacking through tar? No. As you progress, you're supposed to feel more powerful, move faster, traverse back to areas you couldn't and clean up the map.

Instead, it just felt like more slow, dull work with aggravation thrown in here and there, forever at Level 1, never able to actually feel like I was progressing beyond ending levels, all broken up by the occasional boss fight.

It's a Metroidvania in concept alone, it doesn't capture how they're supposed to progress and just throws obsessively perfect challenges at you to compensate. And for that, I'm saying avoid.
Fun.

It's not bad, but it's a bit of a pain to find the hidden treasures throughout previous levels, especially with the map fully revealed.

Fake walls are my least favorite way to hide secrets and this game is rife with them.

[Spoiler]For those that want specifics, after the first boss, keep attacking Andre. Jack will chastise you. Continue this twice-more, and you'll get a shell item that boosts defence.[/Spoiler]

+ This is to state that in addition to [Spoiler]satisfaction, and lore, some of these items have effects.[/Spoiler]

+ While it's separated by levels, these each have their own explorable maps, Order of Ecclesia-style, preserving the Metroid/Castlevania elements, and rewarding exploration.

+ For probably the first time ever in any game of this type, I saw a use for sub weapons.

[h3][b]Meh:[/b][/h3]

~ Semi-odd controls. In spite of most modern controllers having more than 2 buttons, you need to push A + B at-once to jump-dash...and B/O is what the jump button is by default. As everything's rebindable, though, this is a minor issue.

To pause, you also click the right stick, rather than push any traditional button.

[Spoiler]Once you get the materials for it/if you do, the map is accessed via double-tapping up.[/Spoiler]

[h3][b]Nay:[/b][/h3]

- No in-game options menu.

- ...or option to quit out once in.

- Character handling is a bit floaty.

- I would not consider the dialogue to be among the best.

- ...and also think it interrupts things to unnecessarily-large degrees.

- Some of it feels wholly-unnecessary, too, as the instructions for [Spoiler]an out-of-place Quick time event in Level 3/Chapter 2 has the same instruction repeating 3+ times in a row.[/Spoiler] This struck me as player faithlessness.

- Stage 2/second-non-prologue level dials the difficulty up sharply...

- Stage 4 is even worse as you must use a janky “Sniper mode” that doesn't lock your movement to fight owls that bafflingly petrify you on-contact, and demands you use a very inconsistent grappling mechanic on moving hooks that only give you enough height to mount platforms if you time things perfectly...or get lucky.

- This is to type that the enemy powers/status effects make 0 sense to me.

- I also wish they went with more Egyptian-themed enemies, as all of them but two encountered by the give-up point of Stage 5 were animals...

- Yes, you read that right, I stopped even trying to play at Stage 5, which is not only an autoscroller, but requires you to have to jump at the perfect time for pits, throws enemies you need to be perfect to hit at you...then preposterously demands you both beat it without getting hit, and dying, to get all achievements.

I'll spare my sanity of merely beating the level, thank you.

동방 루나 나이츠 등 여러 메트로배니아 게임을 개발한 Team Ladybug의 첫 작품.
큰 기대 없이 플레이했는데 생각보다 되게 재밌었다.



도트 그래픽에서도, 유치한 왕도물 스토리에서도 레트로 게임의 향이 진하게 난다.
레벨 디자인에서도 그러한데, 모든 맵이 서로 연결된 정통 메트로배니아가 아니고 스테이지 식으로 맵이 나뉘어 있음.

하지만 각각의 스테이지가 괜찮은 미니 메트로배니아로 디자인되어 있고, 다른 스테이지와 연관된 어빌리티 게이트와 수집 요소도 잘 배치되어 있어서 장르의 재미는 충분히 느낄 수 있었다.
필요한 위치에 딱딱 배치된 세이브 포인트에서도 개발자의 레벨 디자인 짬이 엿보였음.



조작감이 좋고 캐릭터의 상하 움직임이 가벼워서 액션의 재미가 있었다.
어빌리티를 활용한 플랫포밍도 썩 괜찮고, 수집 요소로 강해지는 정도와 필드 난이도의 균형이 좋아서 전투가 유달리 지루한 구간은 없었다.
무기 디자인과 적 디자인이 잘 되어 있어서 다양한 서브무기를 사용하게 되는 점도 좋았고.

특히, 패턴을 차근차근 익히고 파훼하는 보스전 특유의 성취감을 오랜만에 느낄 수 있어서 좋았다.
다만 최후반 스테이지들은 난이도 곡선이 치솟아서 일정 수준 이상의 수집 요소 파밍이 요구되는 난이도였음. 의도한 것이든 아니든 호불호가 다소 갈릴 만한 요소.



엔딩을 보기 위한 일반적인 플레이에서는 크게 문제되지 않겠지만, 100% 수집 기준으로는 수집 요소가 지나치게 느껴졌다.
개수도 너무 많을 뿐더러, 도저히 공략 없이는 찾기 힘든 위치에 있는 경우가 제법 많았음.
영구적으로 놓칠 수 있는 템도 있고. 게다가 다 모으려면 [spoiler]스테이지 별로 보스 노히트 클리어 해야함...[/spoiler]

그리고 다른 게임 장르로 진행되는 파트가 있는데 많이 별로였다.
더 메신저 DLC도 그렇고, 다른 장르를 오마주할 거면 적당히 맛만 볼 정도로 넣으면 좋을 텐데 왜 뇌절을 하는지 모르겠음...
본편 진행하면서도 지나치다 싶었지만 수집 요소 먹으면서는 더 심했다. 올도과는 더더욱 비추.

기술적인 문제로는 세이브 로드가 너무 느리고, 랙이 너무 자주 걸리더라.
똥컴이긴 하지만 게임 출시연도와 그래픽 퀄리티 치고는 최적화가 너무 구리지 않았나 싶음.



단점들 감안하더라도 개인적으로는 메트로배니아 장르 특유의 재미를 느낄 수 있는 수작이었다.
[u]특히 레트로 감성을 좋아한다면 추천함.[/u]

Short and fun Metroidvania-like game. I like the animations and art style of this one. Not really a true Metroidvania. It's a collection of separate levels with a Metroidvania dungeon layout with a skill upgrade in each level. Lots of secrets and collectibles to get so replaying levels is mandatory to get everything. The way the skills you acquire and the layout of the levels work is you should play each level once then replay them once you have all the upgrades to collect all the missing treasure. You can drop in and out of each level at anytime so there's no need to complete the whole level each time which was a nice feature. Combat is simple enemies just hit harder on harder difficulties nothing special. Platforming and exploring were more engaging than the combat but it's not really a fluid platformer. The driving level really isn't fun at all though I will say that and it drags on too long only to have to fight a boss after it. Not bad 3/5.

1.麻雀虽小，五脏俱全。能力锁流程，收集物很多，并且每个收集物都伴随着能力的提升，让人很有探索的欲望；
2.副武器的设定还蛮有意思的，种类也很多，各有各的用处，整体上虽然没什么打击感但是手感不错，还挺爽的；
3.文本诙谐有趣，有些吐槽很有意思（在此非常感谢汉化组的付出），剧情的话就中规中矩，王道而普通；

一些缺点
1.画面有点过于朴素了，整体给人一种廉价感（虽然实际上也确实很廉价）；
2.初始按键比较难用，虽然支持手柄，但是不能更改映射手柄的按键，并且手柄好像有几个按键是没有对应的，导致有时候还需要额外按键盘；

Cool to see this indie doujin game get a wider release on Steam, especially with it essentially being an early Team Ladybug game, and having a lot of hallmarks of their titles (nice art and animations, fairly story-heavy for the genre).

It's a fun and lighthearted action platformer that I enjoyed my time with - there are some minor Metroidvania elements, like exploring older levels to search for upgrades after getting new abilities, but it feels more like a linear 2d action game for most of its runtime (not a complaint, to be clear). 

My only actual complaint is that stage 5 is an irritating auto-runner level in the vein of the old Donkey Kong Country minecart levels that is far more frustrating than fun; I absolutely could have done without it. It's probably going to put me off from trying to get all the collectibles in the game as well; there are a few in that stage that seem like a nightmare to obtain.

I still had a great time with the other 95% of the game though, absolutely worth spending a few hours with it.

Not too difficult outside of the final boss and extra stage/boss providing a healthy challenge (nothing like crazy kaizo stuff though).

Charming characters, good quality spritework, tight controls, a well managed sense of exploration (while I didn't get everything, I did do some amount of backtracking because I wanted to see what new unlocks/dialogue I could find). 
All around a good experience outside of one particular "on rails" stage involving a car that's pretty tedious.
You may also appreciate it more if you have "tired gamer" syndrome and just want a very classic feeling full-package experience that doesn't overstay its welcome.

An odd hybrid of Metroidvania and more standard action platformers, Pharaoh Rebirth is surprisingly good, yet very overlooked.  This is not a full-fledged Metroidvania, as it is divided into stages, but each stage is fairly large and packed with secrets.  Many of these secrets will be inaccessible until you return with new abilities later in the game, which you will definitely want to do to power yourself up.  I scoured each stage for hidden rooms, but didn't come close to finding them all.  

The action here is fast and frequent, and hard mode can be unforgiving, especially early in the game.  Combat and controls are not quite as polished as some bigger-budget titles, but they get the job done.  There are also a handful of set pieces that offer a change of pace, though one of these - a vehicle chase lined with death traps - does cross into frustration.

I shouldn't have left this one unplayed in my library for so long.  Recommended.

I'd leave a neutral review if I could, it really isn't that bad of a game.

This game is an enhanced paid remake of an obscure freeware sequel to the HYPER obscure Japan-only freeware game "Return Of Egypt", made by the same developer under another pseudonym, from what rare unverifiable information I can find.

It's a relatively common practice for Japanese freeware games to be turned into cheap paid games after being enhanced with extra features once they reach a certain level of popularity, like La-Mulana, which got a full remake that ended up being the version we got in the west. Or any of Studio Pixel's games, or many other examples.

On the off chance you speak Japanese, the original is here: https://www.myabandonware.com/game/return-of-egypt-fvv

This is the only version released in English, but this developer, Krobon Station, would end up forming a team and making the vastly more well known Touhou Luna Nights, and Record of Lodoss War Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth. If you enjoyed either of those, you would enjoy this one, as it has a very similar feel and is on the same engine made by KROBON themselves, the "Mogura Engine", initially made for the shmup game of the same name, "Mogura".

There's a small handful of other games under the "Team Ladybug" umbrella, but those two are the first ones to actually get a release that weren't obscure Japanese freeware. One of their other games, Shin Megami Tensei Synchronicity Prologue, has a fan translation. That game was an officially licensed but fan-made freeware tie-in to Shin Megami Tensei Strange Journey Redux (also known as Deep Strange Journey in Japan).

Onto the actual game, Pharaoh Rebirth has a very La-Mulana derived tone and visual style, but plays much more similarly to the aforementioned games by the same team. Movement is extremely fluid feeling, and attacks have a very well defined and consistent feel to them. One mechanic I found very interesting is how individual items seldom have effects outside of the main treasures and subweapons, but specific sets provide effects when collected, such as a pen, paper, and ink forming your map.

There's not too much to say other than that this is the original game that Team Ladybug's goodness came from.

If you want a number, 8/10. It's VERY good.

EDIT: Turns out the whole item combining thing is done only once in the game, but still, extremely enjoyable Metroidvania, and the collectables still give you stats and some effects.

TLDR: Would I recommend this game? Absolutely, yes.
Would I recommend fully 100%ing it? I was THIS close to doing it, but there's one tiny part of the game that makes me lean more towards a "no" on that.
...More on that later.

Pharaoh Rebirth(+?) is a japanese indie Metroidvania(-ish) game done in a 32-bit era visual style. Y'know, the usual Saturn-type stuff with ridiculously smooth and well drawn spritework, before Sony murdered 2D games in cold blood and the industry never recovered.
The music is up to par too, with tons of catchy high-intensity stuff throughout, plenty of ridiculously catchy basslines to go with it as well.

Now, about the gameplay... I said Metroidvania-ISH because it's not quite one single interconnected map; it's actually a bunch of smaller "levels" each of which are their own self-contained sprawling map that you can explore. You can return to levels at anytime after beating them from the mission select screen though, so no need to worry about missing things (for the most part). It's closer to something like Shantae in that sense, specifically Pirate's Curse and how it was split into "islands".

But yeah, it's basically going off of a platformer base. You run, you jump, you unlock a double-tap sprint later on, as well as double jumping, gliding, and plenty of other useful moves that naturally expand your moveset as you go, allowing you to advance through the game as well as return to previous areas to find extra goodies.

...Now, the main catch here.  The collectibles you find? They're, in a weird way, more loose design-wise but also a lot more organically focused around the game's mechanics. That is a ♥♥♥♥ explanation and I fully know it is.
To go into more detail, EVERY collectible you find adds to your inventory's collection screen, it's this giant WALL of tiles that house the items in question as you find them, in no particular order.

Here's the thing: Some of the items are just that, collectibles that look pretty and are probably valuable in-universe (you're an archeologist, after all), but MOST of them outside of that? They add PASSIVE EFFECTS to your character that just stick around permanently for the rest of your playthrough.
There's the obvious health/mana extensions, those are a staple of the genre, but then there's items that add ENTIRE new properties to your existing moves (like being able to use the slide move in the air, or start a sprint while airborne, or even a weird upgrade for the one-off vehicle stage for some reason). Every item you find MIGHT be another cool upgrade that you don't expect, so it sorta keeps things interesting in its own way.

...Did I mention one of your main moves that's also one of your fastest ways of getting around is essentially a dodge roll/pounce in its own way too? Actually fighting stuff in this game gets SURPRISINGLY deep the later you are into the game, especially as you get to unlock all your moves and subweapons and use them in conjuntion. None of the bosses or enemies really feel cheap either, most damage you end up taking will likely either be because you're learning a boss' pattern or because you were overextending trying to deal damage (that or you mistimed a dodge dash).

I 100%ed the game, got every achievement and collectible and all, relatively fast too.
I just want to also add a tiny little warning... As is a plague for so many platformers, there's a vehicle stage in this game. An obligatory ♥♥♥♥♥♥, one-off, gimmicky, horrendously painful vehicle stage that's genuinely the ONLY part of the game I did not like.
It doesn't last super long and there's ENOUGH checkpoints in it I guess, but the main issue comes when you realize you still have to get collectibles during that entire section. It's an autoscroller where you jump at the right times to not explode and die instantly, and you have to not only NOTICE the collectibles in question (likely miss them), but also ACTUALLY CATCH them. This means you just have to keep killing yourself to go back to wherever the last checkpoint was and try that one jump again.
...You also have to SPEEDRUN that stage for another achievement, which means doing it all in one go WITHOUT using checkpoints because those keep your timer as is instead of resetting it to what it was when you crossed them. If you die you have to quit out to the main menu and reload which takes even longer, just so it doesn't load a checkpoint instead.
Yeah it's just kinda painful.

That unfortunate one single stage aside though (it honestly feels like a dumping ground for all the bad ideas that DIDN'T go into the rest of the game), the game is GENUINELY really really good, especially for how cheap it is.
Let alone if you find it on sale, it's absolutely 100% worth getting.

Impeccable pixel art, fun exploration and platforming, super charming characters and story, it's everything I expect from this developer. KROBON Station/Team Ladybug is now responsible for several of my favorite metroidvanias.

A surprisingly great little Metroidvania/Backtrack Action game. It changes the formula up by having multiple stages with hidden areas or areas you can't access until you've acquired skills in later stages and come back. I really love the character dialogue in between scenes, some seriously funny moments happen. It might seem like a short game, but at the time of this review, I haven't done the extra stages at the end, nor did I try to find all the hidden treasures.

Very enjoyable lite Metroidvania. It's more of a challenging linear story driven platformer with the stages themselves being designed as if they were apart of a bigger Metroidvania game map (similar to Metroid Fusion's level structure but with no main area to walk to the different levels). The story can get in the way since the cutscenses are like the codec calls from MGS (as they happen a lot during gameplay but can be fast forward through) but they can be entertaining and can give characters some development but it's a very predictable story. Overall the game is gorgeous and fun to play, if you like both metroidvanias and linear platforming games (but have a bias towards the linear side of them) I think you will enjoy your time playing this, I definitely did.

The only downsides to this game is a "certain level", and the fact that you only get one savefile. Want to try another difficulty? Say goodbye to your previous saved game.

Other than that, I can't recommend this enough.

I strongly dislike this game! I think there is a good game in here, but it's buried under so many frustrating game decisions that I can't recommend it. 

1. The Dialogue / Lack Of Exploration: My biggest issue is the constant cut scenes. I find the dialogue in this game too cheeky and it robs the player of any of the sense of discovery that makes Metroidvanias great. For example, I stumble upon some fans that aren't running.  A dialogue pops up and says "Hey, I found some fans, but they're not running". "There's a computer nearby where you could get them up and running again and then progress farther". I was able to handle the large amount of dialogue at the beginning, but after 3 hours into the game, there are still way to many cut scenes. For me, it feels like the game treats its players like they're idiots and can't solve a simple puzzle.
2. The Pixel Art / Color Scheme: I almost like the graphics in this game. I don't quite know how to put my finger on it, but the color palette just feels muted. It feels like there's just not quite enough contrast and everything feels dull.
3. Lack Of A Map / Too Linear: This game could really benefit from a map and it feels too linear to be a good Metroidvania. Each level is a self-contained entity and the only reason to back track is to get collectibles.

There are good controls, some solid level design, and some fun bosses, but the negatives far outweigh the positives for me. I don't think I'll be continuing this one anytime soon.

Quite a good game, which is to be expected since the krobon engine (the same thing team ladybug has all its games in) only has good platformers. The music is quite nice, the pixel art is beautiful, enemies and bosses are well designed and rather creative for the most part, the abilities are interesting, and I rather like the characters even if the turtle has a pretty rapid change in characterization. It also successfully pays homage to castlevania, with a few fun references to it with certain items and boss attacks. Does that mean it's perfect? No, because the jeep section is absolutely abysmal and stupid to the point where it alone might drive people to rate it down, and while I like the mission style structure much like the playism konosuba game (minus the shop) fans of the engine's full on metroidvanias may be disappointed by the style (even if each level has a great deal of exploration, optional content, and excellent level structure; sometimes with a good bit of nonlinearity).

One of the best games I've ever played. If you are into exploratory platformers or Metroidvania games, give this a look. While it's level based and the levels are mostly linear, there are tons of secrets and open ended areas. You gain new abilities like a Metroidvania or RPG, but the platforming and combat come first.

The music and graphics are also top notch and the story and characters are great, though there may be a little too much dialogue.

If you like fundamentally good platformers with a focus on returning to old areas with new abilities to find secrets, this game is one of the very best.

[Edit] I want to address some of the concerns I saw on other reviews. First off, the boss rush mode has a pretty significant bug that'll not save your progress unless you hit the accept button super quickly when you get your time at the end.

Secondly, Japanese games don't always play well with American computers, so the initial setup can be annoying. If your controller doesn't work with the game (as mine didn't), you can set up Steam to use your controller to emulate the keyboard for this game.

Also, make sure you check the option to use the D-pad instead of the stick.
